Do NOT look outside this project directory.\\n\\n**Goal**: Understand how the original authors loaded and processed their data.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n- Look for documentation or README files in the `/app/code` directory\\n- Read the provided reference code bases to see how the reference papers loaded and manipulated the data\\n- Understand which functions are being called to read, curate, process, and manipulate the data\\n- For neural imaging data, does delta F over F need to be computed? \\n- For electrophysiology neural data, do cells need to be filtered based on quality? \\n- Note to file important functions, their inputs, and outputs\\n\\n**Done when**: You have documented key functions and their purposes in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 1\\\".\\n\\n**⚠️ CHECKPOINT**: Before proceeding to Step 2, update Step 1 CONVERSION_NOTES.md.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 2: Dataset Exploration\\n\\n**⚠️ CONSTRAINT REMINDER**: Only look at data in the `/app/data` directory. Do NOT look outside this project directory.\\n\\n**Goal**: Understand the native data structure\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n- Identify how data is organized (all files, formats, hierarchies)\\n- Determine available variables and their meanings\\n- Check data dimensions and data types\\n- Look for documentation or README files\\n- Note the data organization and structure\\n- Note dataset size parameters such as the **total number** of subjects (mice), sessions, trials, and neurons\\n\\n**Done when**: You have documented the data structure, file formats, size, and available variables in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 2\\\".\\n\\n**⚠️ CHECKPOINT**: Before proceeding to Step 3, update Step 2 CONVERSION_NOTES.md.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 3: Reference Text Reading\\n\\n**Goal**: Extract key information from the papers and methods.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n- Scan the reference papers and methods.txt for important details about the data\\n- Look for and note to file:\\n  - Any information about dataset size (number of neurons, subjects, sessions, trials)\\n  - Fraction of data with different values, e.g. fraction of rewarded outcomes\\n  - Data processing, curation, and filtering\\n  - Variables important to experiments\\n  - Temporal alignment\\n  - Temporal binning\\n- Read the reference papers to find information about expected decoder accuracy.\\n\\n**Done when**: You have documented expected dataset statistics and processing details in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 3\\\".\\n\\n**⚠️ CHECKPOINT**: Before proceeding to Step 4, update Step 3 CONVERSION_NOTES.md.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 4: Check for Consistency\\n\\n**Goal**: Verify your understanding is consistent across all sources. \\n\\n**Actions**:\\n- Compare your understanding of:\\n  - Important functions from exploring the reference code\\n  - Dataset structure from exploring the dataset\\n  - Analysis described in the reference texts\\n- Note and investigate any discrepancies\\n- In particular, look for discrepancies in:\\n  - Experimental and behavioral variables\\n  - Data processing\\n  - Data curation\\n- Iterate until your understanding of the reference code, dataset, and reference texts are consistent\\n\\n**Done when**: You have resolved all discrepancies and documented your final understanding in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 4\\\".\\n\\n**⚠️ CHECKPOINT**: Before proceeding to Step 5, update Step 4 CONVERSION_NOTES.md.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 5: Mapping Planning\\n\\n**Goal**: Create a detailed plan for mapping source data to target format.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n- Map source data elements to target format components:\\n  - Which variables contain neural activity?\\n  - Identify ALL available experimental variables\\n  - Which variables should be decoder **inputs** vs **outputs**? (Follow Decoder Task section)\\n  - How to discretize continuous outputs (Follow Decoder Task section)\\n  - Which inputs/outputs should be **time-varying** vs **per-trial** (Follow Decoder Task section)\\n  - How does the reference code load and manipulate this data?\\n  - When possible, import or copy code from the reference code in `/app/code` directory. \\n- Consult CONVERSION_NOTES.md under Steps 1-4 and reference materials to determine:\\n  - Temporal binning for spike rates (if applicable)\\n  - Temporal alignment of trials\\n  - Data filtering and curation rules for neurons, trials, and sessions\\n  - Brain regions recorded from\\n- Mapping should be consistent with CONVERSION_NOTES.md under Steps 1-4.\\n- Check for variables indicating valid data periods — exclude invalid data\\n- Note all decisions, edge cases, and data quality issues\\n- Plan and document **sanity and consistency checks** based on dataset size information from the reference texts, code, and data\\n\\n**Done when**:\\n- You have a complete mapping document in CONVERSION_NOTES.md specifying every source-to-target variable mapping under \\\"Step 5\\\"\\n- You have documented all decisions under \\\"Step 5\\\"\\n- You have documented sanity and consistency checks under \\\"Step 5\\\"\\n\\n**⚠️ CHECKPOINT**: Before proceeding to Step 6, update Step 5 CONVERSION_NOTES.md.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 6: Script Development\\n\\n**Goal**: Write the conversion script to `/app/convert_data.py`.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n- Write all conversion code in the file `/app/convert_data.py`\\n- Script should run as **`python -u /app/convert_data.py <outpicklefile>`**\\n- Include options:\\n  - `--full` (default): Process all sessions\\n  - `--sample`: Process only 2 sessions for testing\\n  - `--show-processing`: Plot visualizations of EVERY processing step for up to 2 sessions. Save plots as `processing_<session_id>.png`.\\n- Reuse code from reference code bases where appropriate\\n- Write efficient code:\\n  - Vectorize loops\\n  - Avoid unnecessary file I/O\\n  - Use parallel processing if beneficial\\n  - Print timing information to find bottlenecks\\n- Plots for `--show-processing` mode should visually convince the user that every step of the conversion is correct.\\n  - There are no temporal misalignments\\n  - Discretization of continuous outputs is correct\\n- Write clear, well-documented functions\\n- Handle missing data appropriately (consult references, use sensible defaults, document)\\n- Validate data shapes and types at each step\\n- Include sanity checks (e.g., trial counts match across arrays)\\n\\n**Done when**: `/app/convert_data.py` exists and runs efficiently without errors.\\n\\n**⚠️ DO NOT PROCEED** to Step 7 until `/app/convert_data.py` exists and you have updated Step 6 in CONVERSION_NOTES.md.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 7: Sample Conversion and Validation\\n\\n**Goal**: Validate the conversion on a small sample before processing the full dataset.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n1. Run `python -u /app/convert_data.py /app/sample_data.pkl --sample --show-processing 2>&1 | tee /app/conversion_sample_out.txt`\\n  a. Verify the sample data structure matches the specification.\\n  b. Check dimensions are consistent across trials/sessions.\\n  c. Check that no data is missed during conversion. \\n  d. Validate that metadata accurately describes the data.\\n2. Improve efficiency of conversion.\\n  a. Look at and note timing information for the conversion. \\n  b. Estimate how long the full conversion will run. When you do this, make sure that your estimate accounts for differences in lengths/numbers of trials/sessions. \\n  c. If full conversion time estimate is longer than 15 minutes, speed up the code by writing more efficient code (vectorizing loops, removing unnecessary or redundant computations) and/or including parallel processing. \\n3. Run `python -u /app/train_decoder.py /app/sample_data.pkl --verify-only 2>&1 | tee /app/verification_sample_out.txt`.\\n4. Analyze the output file `/app/verification_sample_out.txt`:\\n  a. Verify no errors reported.\\n  b. Attempt to address any warnings\\n  c. Check input ranges and output value distributions against expectations from reference texts.\\n\\n**Done when**: \\n- `/app/sample_data.pkl` is created and passes manual inspection\\n- `/app/verification_sample_out.txt` is created and passes inspection\\n- Processing plots show no anomalies\\n- Document sample statistics in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 7\\\"\\n\\n**⚠️ DO NOT PROCEED** to Step 8 until `/app/sample_data.pkl` and `/app/verification_sample_out.txt` files exist, and CONVERSION_NOTES.md Step 7 is filled in. \\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 8: Sample Decoder Training\\n\\n**Goal**: Verify the decoder runs successfully on sample data.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n1. Run `python -u /app/train_decoder.py /app/sample_data.pkl 2>&1 | tee /app/train_decoder_sample_out.txt`\\n2. **Check training**: Verify loss decreases over epochs\\n3. **Check accuracy**: Verify accuracy is above chance for EVERY output\\n\\n**Investigate any issues**:\\n- If accuracy is low: check for conversion bugs or reconsider output representation\\n\\n**Done when**: \\n- Decoder training completes without errors\\n- Loss decreases over epochs\\n- Accuracies are above chance\\n- Document all results in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 8\\\"\\n\\n**⚠️ DO NOT PROCEED** to Step 9 until `/app/train_decoder_sample_out.txt` file exists, and CONVERSION_NOTES.md Step 8 is filled in. \\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 9: Full Conversion and Validation\\n\\n**Goal**: Process the complete dataset.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n1. Review your time estimate from Step 7.\\n2. If estimated time is long (e.g. longer than 15 minutes), optimize bottlenecks first.\\n3. Run `python -u /app/convert_data.py /app/converted_data.pkl --full 2>&1 | tee /app/conversion_full_out.txt`\\n4. As the code runs, update your estimates of how long processing will take. If it is much longer than your previous estimate (> 1.5x), kill the process, optimize bottlenecks, and repeat. \\n5. Run `python -u /app/train_decoder.py /app/converted_data.pkl --verify-only 2>&1 | tee /app/verification_full_out.txt`. \\n6. Check that no data was lost during conversion \\n7. Spot-check a few sessions to verify data integrity\\n8. **Check for consistency** between dataset statistics in `/app/verification_full_out.txt` and the reference texts\\n9. Investigate any inconsistencies, and revise the conversion script until all dataset statistics are consistent\\n\\n**Done when**:\\n- `/app/converted_data.pkl` is created and passes manual inspection\\n- `/app/verification_full_out.txt` is created and passes inspection\\n- **ALL** dataset statistics are consistent with values from reference texts\\n- You have documented statistics and consistency in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 9\\\"\\n\\n**⚠️ DO NOT PROCEED** to Step 10 until `/app/converted_data.pkl` and `/app/verification_full_out.txt` files exist and CONVERSION_NOTES.MD Step 9 is filled in.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 10: Critical Review 1\\n\\n**Goal**: Find and fix any errors by performing the following checks. Fix issues and re-run affected steps. Iterate until no issues remain.\\n\\n**Check 1: Output log verification**\\nRead through `/app/verification_full_out.txt` to find and fix **all errors**. Address each warning by either fixing its cause or verifying it that it is not possible to fix it. Explain why each warning could not be fixed in `/app/CONVERSION_NOTES.md`. \\n\\n**Check 2: Construct sanity checks**\\n- Develop at least one sanity check each on neural, input, and output data.\\n- These must involve loading in the original data files (NOT through your conversion code).\\n- Construct comparison tests and criteria using `np.allclose()`. \\n- These tests can be spot-checks of the data, e.g. neural activity at trial 5, timepoint 10, neuron 3. \\n- Fix all mismatches/sanity check failures. \\n- Document your sanity checks to `/app/CONVERSION_NOTES.md`. \\n\\n**Check 3: Reference code comparison**\\n- Compare your code to the reference code and methods. \\n- For each major processing step — (a) data loading, (b) neuron/trial filtering, (c) temporal alignment, (d) binning, (e) input construction, (f) output construction — identify the corresponding code in your script and in the reference, and compare the logic. \\n- Check whether you use the same variables, filtering, and processing as the reference code. \\n- Fix any mismatches. \\n- Document your comparisons in `/app/CONVERSION_NOTES.md`. \\n- Explain your reasoning for any differences in `/app/CONVERSION_NOTES.md`.\\n\\n**Check 4: Key statistics comparison**\\n- Verify that key statistics (number of animals, sessions, trials, neurons, input and output ranges, output distributions) match information available in the reference papers. \\n- Write code to investigate any discrepancies. \\n- Fix any discovered issues. \\n- Document your comparisons in `/app/CONVERSION_NOTES.md`. \\n\\n**Check 5: Check for edge cases**\\n- Check for off-by-one errors at the beginning/ends of trials, sessions, and subjects, or in definitions of the inputs and outputs. \\n- There may be minor issues in the data that your code must handle. Check that your code robustly handles issues in the original data. \\n\\n**Iteration protocol**: If ANY check above reveals an issue:\\n1. Fix the issue in convert_data.py\\n2. Re-run the affected conversion and validation steps\\n3. Re-run ALL checks in this step (not just the one that failed)\\n4. Document each iteration: what was found, what was fixed, what the re-check showed\\n\\nWrite a report to CONVERSION_NOTES.md describing **every** check you did, to help convince the user that the conversion code works. **Done when**: You have documented your review findings and all issues are resolved in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 10\\\".\\n\\n**⚠️ DO NOT PROCEED** to Step 11 until you have checked for consistency between **every** statistic in the reference texts, code, and data and documented in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under Step 10. \\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 11: Full Decoder Training\\n\\n**Goal**: Validate the decoder on the **complete** dataset.\\n\\n**⚠️ IMPORTANT**: This step must complete fully. Do not skip or abbreviate. Do not proceed to Step 12 until this step is completely finished.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n1. Run `python -u /app/train_decoder.py /app/converted_data.pkl --plot-samples 2>&1 | tee /app/train_decoder_full_out.txt`. If the GPU does not have sufficient RAM for the network training, use the flag `--cpu` to specify to use the CPU to train. \\n2. **Wait for complete execution** — this may take significant time for large datasets\\n3. **Check training**: Verify loss decreases over epochs\\n4. **Check accuracy**: High accuracy is an indicator that data conversion has been done correctly. Accuracy near chance is a sign that there might be issues in temporal alignment of signals, choice of data streams, or filtering or processing of data. Compare accuracy to expectations based on the papers. \\n\\n**Done when**: \\n1. Full decoder training completes (the script finishes running)\\n2. Accuracy results are documented in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 11\\\" with a table of accuracies\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 12: Critical Review 2\\n\\n**Goal**: Find and fix any errors by performing the following checks. Fix issues and re-run affected steps. Iterate until no issues remain. Perform all of the following checks:\\n\\n**Check 1: Accuracy vs chance analysis**\\n- For each output, compare validation accuracy to chance (1/num_classes)\\n- Accuracy below chance indicates a bug, investigate and fix conversion issues to improve this. \\n- Accuracy below 1.5x chance may also indicate a bug, investigate whether changes in conversion logic could improve accuracy. \\n\\n**Check 2: Accuracy comparison to papers**\\n- Find every decoding accuracy reported in the reference papers\\n- Create a table comparing your accuracy to the papers' accuracy for each variable\\n- If your accuracy is lower than the reported accuracy, this may indicate a bug in your conversion that you must fix. \\n- Differences in algorithm/architecture should be relatively small because of the data dimensionality and size. Do not use this as an excuse to dismiss differences, investigate them completely before moving on. \\n\\n**Check 3: Train vs validation gap**\\n- If training accuracy is much higher (>1.5x) than validation accuracy for any output, investigate overfitting or data leakage. \\n\\n**If accuracy is low for an output, try these specific debugging steps:**\\n1. Verify the output values are correct by loading raw data and checking 3 specific trials\\n2. Check temporal alignment — plot neural + output for a single trial to verify they're synchronized\\n3. Check whether the output has enough variation (not 99% one class)\\n4. Check that filtering steps for neural activity streams are followed. \\n5. Check that processing of the data matches the reference code and papers. \\n\\n**Iteration protocol**: If ANY check above reveals an issue:\\n1. Fix the issue in convert_data.py\\n2. Re-run the affected conversion and validation steps\\n3. Re-run ALL checks in this step (not just the one that failed)\\n4. Document each iteration: what was found, what was fixed, what the re-check showed\\n\\n**Report all checks and results** to `/app/CONVERSION_NOTES.md` to convince the user that the conversion and decoding has been done correctly. \\n\\n**Done when**: You have documented your review findings and all issues are resolved in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 12\\\".\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 13: Documentation and Cleanup\\n\\n**Goal**: Finalize documentation and organize files.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n- Ensure CONVERSION_NOTES.md is complete with all:\\n  - Key decisions and rationale\\n  - Checks for correctness of the conversion\\n  - Validation results and tables\\n  - Any issues found and how they were resolved\\n- Create a user-facing `/app/README.md` summarizing:\\n  - Dataset description\\n  - How to load and use the converted data\\n  - Output format specification\\n  - Key statistics\\n- Move analysis/investigation scripts to a `/app/cache/` folder\\n- Create `/app/cache/README_CACHE.md` documenting cached files\\n\\n**Done when**: README.md exists, CONVERSION_NOTES.md is complete, and directory is clean.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## CONVERSION_NOTES.md Template\\n\\n**Create this file IMMEDIATELY in Step 0.            \"content\": \"1→Behavior and video tracking\\n     2→\\n     3→Mice performed an auditory delayed response task 21 (Figure 1A). The instruction stimuli during the sample epoch were pure tones played at one of two frequencies (3 kHz or 12 kHz). Each tone was played three times for 150 ms with 100 ms inter-tone intervals. The sample epoch was followed by a 1.2 s delay epoch. An auditory ‘Go’ cue (carrier frequency of 6 kHz with 360 Hz modulating fre-\\n     4→quency, 0.1 s duration) indicated the end of the delay epoch. Licking early during the sample/delay epoch triggered a replay of the epoch. During the response epoch (answer period: 1.5 s) mice reported the instruction by licking one of the two lick ports. Licking (consumption period: 1.5 s) the correct lick port triggered a small water reward (0.1 ~ 0.2 ul). Licking the incorrect lick port triggered a timeout (1-3 s). After mice stopped licking for 1.5 s, the trial ended, followed by a 250 ms inter-trial-interval. Early lick trials and no\\n     5→response trials were excluded for analysis. Overall performance was computed as the fraction of correct control trials (i.e. no photostimulation), excluding any early lick trials. We selected experimental sessions for analysis based on following criteria: overall behavioral performance (> 65%), and at least 50 correct lick left and lick right trials each. Mice performed on average 476 (Mean; range, 130-785) trials per session with 84% correct rate (range, 65-99%; STAR Methods). During the delay epoch, mice maintain a memory of their choice and plan a movement.\\n     6→\\n     7→Two CMOS cameras (CM3-U3-13Y3M, FLIR) were used to track orofacial movements of the mouse under IR light illumination (940 nm LED). The cameras were equipped with 4-12 mm focal length lenses (12VM412ASIR, Tamron) and a pixel resolution of 71 mm. High-speed videos from a side view and a bottom view (Figure 1C) were acquired at 300 Hz using software FlyCapture (TELEDYNE FLIR). We trained DeepLabCut 39 to track the movement of tongue, jaw and nose (Figure 1I).\\n     8→\\n     9→Multi-regional electrophysiological recordings\\n    10→\\n    11→We designed a ﬂexible manipulator system for multiple Neuropixels probe insertions (https://www.janelia.org/open-science/manipulator-system-for-multiple-neuropixels-probe-recordings). Three to four small craniotomies (diameter, 1 \\u0018 1.5 mm) were made over target brain areas one day before the ﬁrst recording session. Details of recordings made with multiple Neuropixels probes in head-restrained behaving animals have been published (dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8tphwmn). Target regions, insertions angles, probe types, etc. are summarized in Table S2. All coordinates are given with respect to Bregma (AP, anterior-posterior; ML, medial-lateral; DV, dorsal-ventral).\\n    12→\\n    13→Extracellular spikes were recorded using Neuropixels 1.0 probes, 2.0 single-shank (SS) and 2.0 multi-shank (MS) probes 3,4 (Table S2). Three to seven recordings were made from each craniotomy. Recording depth was inferred from manipulator readings (Sensapax uMp manipulators). After completion of probe insertion, brain tissue was allowed to settle for several minutes before recording. During recordings the craniotomies were immersed in saline.\\n    14→\\n    15→Probes were conﬁgured and data were visualized and streamed to disk using the open-source software package SpikeGLX (https://billkarsh.github.io/SpikeGLX/). Data from up to ﬁve simultaneously recorded probes were acquired at 30 kHz. Sync waves (0.5 s duty cycle TTL pulses) were recorded across probes and on auxiliary channels for synchronization.\\n    16→\\n    17→Photoinhibition\\n    18→\\n    19→Light from two 473 nm lasers (Coherent OBIS LS/LX) was used to illuminate the two hemispheres of ALM. The laser power was controlled by analog outputs controlled by a Bpod (Sanworks). Photoinactivation of ALM (centered on AP 2.5 mm; ML 1.5 mm) was performed through clear-skull cap implant11 or via craniotomy by directing the laser over the skull (beam diameter, 1.8 mm at 4 sigma). Photoinhibition of the left-, right-ALM hemisphere, or both hemispheres was deployed on a subset of ~25% randomly interleaved trials 11,21 (N = 17 VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice). To prevent the mice from distinguishing photostimulation trials from control rials using visual cues, a ‘masking ﬂash’ (1 ms pulses at 10 Hz) was delivered using 470 nm LEDs in front of the mice throughout the entire trial. For silencing ALM, we stimulated cortical GABAergic neurons in VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice. We used 40 Hz photostimulation with a sinusoidal temporal proﬁle (5 mW average power per hemisphere) and a 100 ms linear ramping down during the laser offset to reduce rebound neuronal activity. This photo stimulus is expected to silence glutamatergic neurons in all of ALM. 37 We silenced ALM activity during the late delay epoch (last 0.5 s), including the 100 ms ramp-down. Thus, photoinhibition always ended before the ‘Go’ cue.\\n    20→\\n    21→To analyze the effects of photoinhibition, units with at least 10 photostimulation trials were selected for analysis (Figures 5 and S5). Bilateral ALM photostimulation reduced behavior performance from 83.2% to 71.7% (N = 17 VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice, n = 93 sessions). To exclude the effects of rebound population activity in the thalamus 16 and other subcortical regions, we used a 20-120 ms\\n    22→time window after photo stimulation onset to measure the effect of ALM inactivation in downstream regions (Figures 5 and S5). For ALM itself, we used 500 ms (i.e. the entire inactivation period) to calculate spike rate reduction.\\n    23→\\n    24→Spike sorting and quality control\\n    25→\\n    26→We developed a data pipeline for preprocessing, spike sorting and quality control (https://github.com/jenniferColonell/ecephys_spike_sorting). The extracellular recording traces were ﬁrst band-pass ﬁltered (Butterworth acausal ﬁlter, 250 Hz - 9 kHz). We then sorted the dataset using both Kilosort2 32 (MATLAB version, GitHub - jenniferColonell/KS20_for_preprocessed_data: Release version of KS2 for preprocessed data) and Kilosort2.5 4 (Python version, GitHub - jenniferColonell/pykilosort: [WIP] Python port of Kilosort 2). Both sorting methods gave similar results. In the analyses presented in the paper, we used the output from Kilosort2. Each output cluster was associated with a list of 15 quality metrics calculated to assess isolation and sorting quality 7 (i.e. quality control) (https://github.com/AllenInstitute/ecephys_spike_sorting/tree/master/ecephys_spike_sorting/modules/quality_metrics).\\n    27→\\n    28→The details of the spike sorting and quality control are described in an accompanying white paper (https://doi.org/10.25378/janelia.24066108.v1). In brief, we used 15 cluster quality metrics to train classiﬁers - one for each of the major ﬁve brain areas (cortex, striatum, thalamus, midbrain and medulla). The classiﬁers were trained based on labels derived from manual curation. We curated Kilosort2 output (28 penetrations from ﬁve brain areas) using the open-source graphical user interface Phy (GitHub - cortex-lab/phy: phy: interactive visualization and manual spike sorting of large-scale ephys data). Each cluster was labeled as a ‘good’ or ‘unlabeled’ unit. Annotators were blind to location, recording condition and trial type information. Based on the annotated labels of all clusters and associated quality metrics, we trained ﬁve region-speciﬁc classiﬁers using logistic regression. Applying the trained classiﬁers to the rest of the dataset provided lists of units that were labeled as ‘good’ and were used for the analysis in this paper. We applied the cortex classiﬁer to ALM and other cortex, hippocampus, olfactory and cortical subplate units; the striatum classiﬁer to striatum and pallidum units; the thalamus classiﬁer to thalamus and hypothalamus units; the midbrain classiﬁer to midbrain and pons units; the medulla classiﬁer to medulla and cerebellum units. We calculated the rate at which the classiﬁer incorrectly labeled ’unlabeled’ units as ’good’, using 10-fold cross-validation on held-out manually labeled units (false alarm rate): 7.8%; striatum: 6.4%; thalamus: 7.3%; midbrain: 5.5%; medulla 4.3%. This method yielded 8717 good units from ALM, 7664 from striatum, 12808 from thalamus, 7495 from midbrain and 2928 from medulla, etc. Overall, the dataset consisted of 69,943 good units recorded across 173 behavioral sessions, from which 655 probe insertions were made. To exclude the effects of rebound population activity in the thalamus 16 and other subcortical regions, we used a 20-120 ms\\ntime window after photo stimulation onset to measure the effect of ALM inactivation in downstream regions (Figures 5 and S5). For ALM itself, we used 500 ms (i.e. the entire inactivation period) to calculate spike rate reduction.\\n\\nSpike sorting and quality control\\n\\nWe developed a data pipeline for preprocessing, spike sorting and quality control (https://github.com/jenniferColonell/ecephys_spike_sorting). The extracellular recording traces were ﬁrst band-pass ﬁltered (Butterworth acausal ﬁlter, 250 Hz - 9 kHz). We then sorted the dataset using both Kilosort2 32 (MATLAB version, GitHub - jenniferColonell/KS20_for_preprocessed_data: Release version of KS2 for preprocessed data) and Kilosort2.5 4 (Python version, GitHub - jenniferColonell/pykilosort: [WIP] Python port of Kilosort 2). Both sorting methods gave similar results. In the analyses presented in the paper, we used the output from Kilosort2. Each output cluster was associated with a list of 15 quality metrics calculated to assess isolation and sorting quality 7 (i.e. quality control) (https://github.com/AllenInstitute/ecephys_spike_sorting/tree/master/ecephys_spike_sorting/modules/quality_metrics).\\n\\nThe details of the spike sorting and quality control are described in an accompanying white paper (https://doi.org/10.25378/janelia.24066108.v1). In brief, we used 15 cluster quality metrics to train classiﬁers - one for each of the major ﬁve brain areas (cortex, striatum, thalamus, midbrain and medulla). The classiﬁers were trained based on labels derived from manual curation. We curated Kilosort2 output (28 penetrations from ﬁve brain areas) using the open-source graphical user interface Phy (GitHub - cortex-lab/phy: phy: interactive visualization and manual spike sorting of large-scale ephys data). Each cluster was labeled as a ‘good’ or ‘unlabeled’ unit. Annotators were blind to location, recording condition and trial type information. Based on the annotated labels of all clusters and associated quality metrics, we trained ﬁve region-speciﬁc classiﬁers using logistic regression. Applying the trained classiﬁers to the rest of the dataset provided lists of units that were labeled as ‘good’ and were used for the analysis in this paper. We applied the cortex classiﬁer to ALM and other cortex, hippocampus, olfactory and cortical subplate units; the striatum classiﬁer to striatum and pallidum units; the thalamus classiﬁer to thalamus and hypothalamus units; the midbrain classiﬁer to midbrain and pons units; the medulla classiﬁer to medulla and cerebellum units. We calculated the rate at which the classiﬁer incorrectly labeled ’unlabeled’ units as ’good’, using 10-fold cross-validation on held-out manually labeled units (false alarm rate): 7.8%; striatum: 6.4%; thalamus: 7.3%; midbrain: 5.5%; medulla 4.3%. This method yielded 8717 good units from ALM, 7664 from striatum, 12808 from thalamus, 7495 from midbrain and 2928 from medulla, etc. Overall, the dataset consisted of 69,943 good units recorded across 173 behavioral sessions, from which 655 probe insertions were made. Both have the same t-score, but p_value(2-tailed) = 2*p_value(1-tailed).\\n   292→\\n   293→    Returns:\\n   294→        t_score (adarray or scaler): dimension same as the '...' of x1 or x2.\\n   295→        pval (adarray or scaler): dimension same as t_score\\n   296→    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n   297→    n1 = x1.shape[-1]\\n   298→    n2 = x2.shape[-1]\\n   299→    df = n1 +n2 - 2 # degree of freedom\\n   300→\\n   301→    Sp = ( (n1-1)*np.var(x1,axis=-1) + (n2-1)*np.var(x2,axis=-1) ) / df\\n   302→    s = np.sqrt(Sp*(1/n1 + 1/n2))\\n   303→\\n   304→    t_score = (np.mean(x2, axis=-1) - np.mean(x1, axis=-1)) / s # （n_bins,n_neurons）\\n   305→    # if isinstance(a, np.array): # not scalar\\n   306→    #     t_score[np.isnan(t_score)] = 0 # sometimes Sp=0 (since var=0). This is to deal with cases where for e.g. (bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride is actually 43 but evaluates to 42.999999... due to numerical errors in floating-point arithmetic.\\\\n    if np.allclose((bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride, math.floor((bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride)+1):\\\\n        n_bins =  math.floor((bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride)+2\\\\n    else:\\\\n        n_bins = math.floor((bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride)+1\\\\n    binCenters = bin_begin_time + np.arange(n_bins)*stride\\\\n\\\\n    binIntervals = np.vstack((binCenters-bin_width/2, binCenters+bin_width/2)).T\\\\n\\\\n    # This is to deal with cases where for e.g. (bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride is actually 43 but evaluates to 42.999999... due to numerical errors in floating-point arithmetic.\\n    45→    if np.allclose((bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride, math.floor((bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride)+1):\\n    46→        n_bins =  math.floor((bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride)+2\\n    47→    else:\\n    48→        n_bins = math.floor((bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride)+1\\n    49→    binCenters = bin_begin_time + np.arange(n_bins)*stride\\n    50→\\n    51→    binIntervals = np.vstack((binCenters-bin_width/2, binCenters+bin_width/2)).T\\n    52→\\n    53→    # Count number of spikes for each sliding bin\\n    54→    binSpikes = np.asarray([[[np.sum(np.all([trial>=binInt[0], trial<binInt[1]], axis=0)) for binInt in binIntervals] for trial in unit]\\n    55→        for unit in spikeTimes]).swapaxes(0,-1)\\n    56→\\n    57→    if rate:\\n    58→        return binCenters, binSpikes/float(bin_width) # Empty 0x1 cell. Need to manually define what it becomes in Python.\\n2. 1x1 cell. Will be directly read as non-iterables such as str, int, float, etc. Need to manually convert it to an iterable with length 1.\\n3. Nx1 cell (N >= 2). Usually it's fine to read and directly store it in Python.\\n\\nComment: in case 2, when using isinstance(data, data_type), if data could be a number, consider the possibility of data being either float or int, i.e. use\\n    if isinstance(data, float) or isinstance(data, int):\\n        do something\\n\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\nplt.rcParams['pdf.fonttype'] = 42\\nplt.rcParams['ps.fonttype'] = 42\\n\\n\\ndef sliding_histogram(spikeTimes, begin_time, end_time, bin_width, stride, rate=True):\\n    '''\\n    Calculates the number of spikes for each unit in each sliding bin of width bin_width, strided by stride.\\n    begin_time and end_time are treated as the lower- and upper- bounds for bin centers.\\n    if rate=True, calculate firing rates instead of bin spikes.\\n    '''\\n    bin_begin_time = begin_time\\n    bin_end_time = end_time\\n    # This is to deal with cases where for e.g. (bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride is actually 43 but evaluates to 42.999999... due to numerical errors in floating-point arithmetic.\\n    if np.allclose((bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride, math.floor((bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride)+1):\\n        n_bins =  math.floor((bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride)+2\\n    else:\\n        n_bins = math.floor((bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride)+1\\n    binCenters = bin_begin_time + np.arange(n_bins)*stride\\n\\n    binIntervals = np.vstack((binCenters-bin_width/2, binCenters+bin_width/2)).T\\n\\n    # This is to deal with cases where for e.g. (bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride is actually 43 but evaluates to 42.999999... due to numerical errors in floating-point arithmetic.\\n    45→    if np.allclose((bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride, math.floor((bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride)+1):\\n    46→        n_bins =  math.floor((bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride)+2\\n    47→    else:\\n    48→        n_bins = math.floor((bin_end_time-bin_begin_time)/stride)+1\\n    49→    binCenters = bin_begin_time + np.arange(n_bins)*stride\\n    50→\\n    51→    binIntervals = np.vstack((binCenters-bin_width/2, binCenters+bin_width/2)).T\\n    52→\\n    53→    # Count number of spikes for each sliding bin\\n    54→    binSpikes = np.asarray([[[np.sum(np.all([trial>=binInt[0], trial<binInt[1]], axis=0)) for binInt in binIntervals] for trial in unit]\\n    55→        for unit in spikeTimes]).swapaxes(0,-1)\\n    56→\\n    57→    if rate:\\n    58→        return binCenters, binSpikes/float(bin_width) # keyword-based groups\\n    for kw in THALAMUS_KEYWORDS:\\n        if kw in anno_name:\\n            return 'TH'\\n    for kw in MIDBRAIN_KEYWORDS:\\n        if kw in anno_name:\\n            return 'MB'\\n    for kw in PONS_KEYWORDS:\\n        if kw in anno_name:\\n            return 'Pons'\\n    for kw in MEDULLA_KEYWORDS:\\n        if kw in anno_name:\\n            return 'MY'\\n    for kw in CEREBELLUM_KEYWORDS:\\n        if kw in anno_name:\\n            return 'CB'\\n    for kw in HIPPOCAMPUS_KEYWORDS:\\n        if kw in anno_name:\\n            return 'HPF'\\n    for kw in OLFACTORY_KEYWORDS:\\n        if kw in anno_name:\\n            return 'OLF'\\n    for kw in CORTICAL_SUBPLATE_KEYWORDS:\\n        if kw in anno_name:\\n            return 'CTXsp'\\n\\n    # Cortex catch-all (layer annotations)\\n    if 'layer' in anno_name.lower() or 'Layer' in anno_name:\\n        return 'CTX_other'\\n\\n    # Striatum catch-all\\n    if 'striatum' in anno_name.lower() or 'Striatum' in anno_name:\\n        return 'STR'\\n\\n    return 'unknown'\\n\\n\\ndef extract_unit_spike_times(spike_times_data, spike_times_index, unit_indices):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Extract spike times for multiple units at once.\\n    Returns list of arrays, one per unit.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    starts = np.zeros(len(unit_indices), dtype=np.int64)\\n    ends = spike_times_index[unit_indices].astype(np.int64)\\n    for i, idx in enumerate(unit_indices):\\n        if idx == 0:\\n            starts[i] = 0\\n        else:\\n            starts[i] = int(spike_times_index[idx - 1])\\n    return [spike_times_data[starts[i]:ends[i]] for i in range(len(unit_indices))]\\n\\n\\ndef compute_firing_rates_fast(unit_spike_times_list, go_times, bin_edges):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Compute firing rates for all units and trials.\\n    Optimized: iterate over units (outer) and vectorize across trials.\\n    Returns list of (n_units, n_bins) arrays, one per trial.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    n_units = len(unit_spike_times_list)\\n    n_bins = len(bin_edges) - 1\\n    bin_width = bin_edges[1] - bin_edges[0]\\n    n_trials = len(go_times)\\n\\n    # Pre-allocate result as 3D array, then split\\n    all_rates = np.zeros((n_units, n_trials, n_bins), dtype=np.float32)\\n\\n    for ni in range(n_units):\\n        st = unit_spike_times_list[ni]\\n        if len(st) == 0:\\n            continue\\n\\n        for ti in range(n_trials):\\n            go_t = go_times[ti]\\n            t_lo = go_t + bin_edges[0]\\n            t_hi = go_t + bin_edges[-1]\\n            i_lo = np.searchsorted(st, t_lo)\\n            i_hi = np.searchsorted(st, t_hi)\\n            if i_lo >= i_hi:\\n                continue\\n            # np.histogram is C-optimized and faster than searchsorted+add.at\\n            counts, _ = np.histogram(st[i_lo:i_hi], bins=bin_edges + go_t)\\n            all_rates[ni, ti] = counts\\n\\n    all_rates /= bin_width\\n\\n    # Split into list of per-trial arrays\\n    return [all_rates[:, ti, :] for ti in range(n_trials)]\\n\\n\\ndef find_tone_onset_for_trial(sample_start_times, go_time):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Find the last sample_start before the go cue for this trial.\\n    This accounts for epoch replays due to early licks.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    candidates = sample_start_times[sample_start_times < go_time]\\n    if len(candidates) == 0:\\n        # Fallback: assume standard timing (sample = 0.65s + delay = 1.2s before go)\\n        return go_time - 1.85\\n    return candidates[-1]\\n\\n\\ndef get_photostim_intervals(f, n_trials, go_times, trial_start_times):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Get photostim intervals relative to go cue for each trial.\\n    Returns list of (onset_rel, offset_rel) or None for each trial.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    photostim_onset = f['intervals']['trials']['photostim_onset'][:]\\n    photostim_dur = f['intervals']['trials']['photostim_duration'][:]\\n\\n    intervals = []\\n    for i in range(n_trials):\\n        if photostim_onset[i] == b'N/A':\\n            intervals.append(None)\\n        else:\\n            onset_rel_trial = float(photostim_onset[i])\\n            dur = float(photostim_dur[i])\\n            # Convert from trial-relative to go-cue-relative\\n            onset_abs = onset_rel_trial + trial_start_times[i]\\n            onset_rel_go = onset_abs - go_times[i]\\n            offset_rel_go = onset_rel_go + dur\\n            intervals.append((onset_rel_go, offset_rel_go))\\n    return intervals\\n\\n\\ndef compute_tongue_y_all_trials(tongue_ts, tongue_data, go_times, bin_edges,\\n                                 likelihood_thresh=TONGUE_LIKELIHOOD_THRESH):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Compute discretized tongue y-position for all trials using vectorized operations.\\n    Returns (tongue_discretized_list, p40, p60).\\n    Categories: 0=<40th, 1=40-60th, 2=>60th, 3=not visible\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    tongue_y = tongue_data[:, 1]\\n    tongue_lh = tongue_data[:, 2]\\n    n_bins = len(bin_edges) - 1\\n    n_trials = len(go_times)\\n    bin_width = bin_edges[1] - bin_edges[0]\\n\\n    # Pre-compute bin assignments for tongue timestamps\\n    # For each trial, we need tongue data in [go_time + T_START, go_time + T_END]\\n    # Use searchsorted for fast indexing\\n\\n    # First pass: collect visible y values for percentile computation\\n    visible_y_all = []\\n    # For each trial, find tongue data indices\\n    trial_tongue_ranges = []\\n    for ti in range(n_trials):\\n        go_t = go_times[ti]\\n        t_lo = go_t + bin_edges[0]\\n        t_hi = go_t + bin_edges[-1]\\n        i_lo = np.searchsorted(tongue_ts, t_lo)\\n        i_hi = np.searchsorted(tongue_ts, t_hi)\\n        trial_tongue_ranges.append((i_lo, i_hi))\\n\\n        if i_lo < i_hi:\\n            vis_mask = tongue_lh[i_lo:i_hi] >= likelihood_thresh\\n            if vis_mask.any():\\n                visible_y_all.append(tongue_y[i_lo:i_hi][vis_mask])\\n\\n    if len(visible_y_all) == 0:\\n        p40, p60 = None, None\\n        return [np.full(n_bins, 3, dtype=np.int64) for _ in range(n_trials)], p40, p60\\n\\n    all_visible = np.concatenate(visible_y_all)\\n    p40 = np.percentile(all_visible, 40)\\n    p60 = np.percentile(all_visible, 60)\\n\\n    # Second pass: discretize tongue y per trial and bin\\n    results = []\\n    for ti in range(n_trials):\\n        go_t = go_times[ti]\\n        i_lo, i_hi = trial_tongue_ranges[ti]\\n        trial_bins = np.full(n_bins, 3, dtype=np.int64)\\n\\n        if i_lo >= i_hi:\\n            results.append(trial_bins)\\n            continue\\n\\n        # Get tongue data for this trial\\n        trial_ts = tongue_ts[i_lo:i_hi]\\n        trial_y = tongue_y[i_lo:i_hi]\\n        trial_lh = tongue_lh[i_lo:i_hi]\\n\\n        # Assign each tongue sample to a bin\\n        rel_ts = trial_ts - go_t\\n        bin_idx = np.searchsorted(bin_edges, rel_ts, side='right') - 1\\n        valid = (bin_idx >= 0) & (bin_idx < n_bins)\\n\\n        if not valid.any():\\n            results.append(trial_bins)\\n            continue\\n\\n        bin_idx_v = bin_idx[valid]\\n        trial_y_v = trial_y[valid]\\n        trial_lh_v = trial_lh[valid]\\n\\n        # Compute mean y and mean likelihood per bin using bincount\\n        for b in range(n_bins):\\n            b_mask = bin_idx_v == b\\n            if not b_mask.any():\\n                continue\\n            avg_lh = trial_lh_v[b_mask].mean()\\n            if avg_lh >= likelihood_thresh:\\n                avg_y = trial_y_v[b_mask].mean()\\n                if avg_y < p40:\\n                    trial_bins[b] = 0\\n                elif avg_y <= p60:\\n                    trial_bins[b] = 1\\n                else:\\n                    trial_bins[b] = 2\\n\\n        results.append(trial_bins)\\n    return results, p40, p60\\n\\n\\ndef process_session(nwb_path, show_processing=False):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Process a single NWB session file.\\n    Returns session data dict or None if session should be skipped.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    t0 = time.time()\\n    basename = os.path.basename(nwb_path)\\n\\n    f = h5py.File(nwb_path, 'r')\\n\\n    # ── Subject info ──\\n    subject_id = f['general']['subject']['subject_id'][()].decode()\\n\\n    # ── Trial info ──\\n    n_trials_total = f['intervals']['trials']['id'].shape[0]\\n    outcome = np.array([x.decode() for x in f['intervals']['trials']['outcome'][:]])\\n    early_lick = np.array([x.decode() for x in f['intervals']['trials']['early_lick'][:]])\\n    trial_instruction = np.array([x.decode() for x in f['intervals']['trials']['trial_instruction'][:]])\\n    auto_water = f['intervals']['trials']['auto_water'][:]\\n    free_water = f['intervals']['trials']['free_water'][:]\\n    photostim_power = f['intervals']['trials']['photostim_power'][:]\\n    trial_start_times = f['intervals']['trials']['start_time'][:]\\n\\n    # ── Session selection ──\\n    # The DANDI archive already contains sessions selected by the paper authors\\n    # (performance > 65%, >= 50 correct L and R trials). One session has no good units.\\n    is_auto_or_free = (auto_water == 1) | (free_water == 1)\\n\\n    # Compute performance for metadata (on control non-early-lick trials)\\n    is_control = (photostim_power == b'N/A') & (early_lick == 'no early') & ~is_auto_or_free\\n    n_control_responded = np.sum((outcome[is_control] == 'hit') | (outcome[is_control] == 'miss'))\\n    n_correct = np.sum(outcome[is_control] == 'hit')\\n    performance = n_correct / n_control_responded if n_control_responded > 0 else 0\\n\\n    # ── Trial filtering: remove auto_water and free_water ──\\n    trial_mask = ~is_auto_or_free\\n    trial_indices = np.where(trial_mask)[0]\\n    n_trials = len(trial_indices)\\n\\n    if n_trials < 2:\\n        print(f\\\"  SKIP {basename}: only {n_trials} valid trials\\\")\\n        f.close()\\n        return None\\n\\n    # ── Go cue times ──\\n    go_start_times = f['acquisition']['BehavioralEvents']['go_start_times']['timestamps'][:]\\n    assert len(go_start_times) == n_trials_total, f\\\"Go cue count mismatch: {len(go_start_times)} vs {n_trials_total}\\\"\\n    go_times = go_start_times[trial_indices]\\n    trial_starts = trial_start_times[trial_indices]\\n\\n    # ── Good units ──\\n    classification = f['units']['classification'][:]\\n    good_mask = classification == b'good'\\n    good_indices = np.where(good_mask)[0]\\n    n_good = len(good_indices)\\n\\n    if n_good == 0:\\n        print(f\\\"  SKIP {basename}: no good units\\\")\\n        f.close()\\n        return None\\n\\n    # ── Brain region annotations ──\\n    anno_names = f['units']['anno_name'][:]\\n    good_annos = [anno_names[i].decode() if isinstance(anno_names[i], bytes) else str(anno_names[i])\\n                  for i in good_indices]\\n    good_regions = [classify_brain_region(a) for a in good_annos]\\n\\n    # ── Spike times ──\\n    spike_times_data = f['units']['spike_times'][:]\\n    spike_times_index = f['units']['spike_times_index'][:]\\n\\n    # Extract spike times for all good units once\\n    unit_spike_times = extract_unit_spike_times(spike_times_data, spike_times_index, good_indices)\\n\\n    # Compute firing rates for all good units and trials\\n    neural_data = compute_firing_rates_fast(unit_spike_times, go_times, BIN_EDGES)\\n\\n    # ── Inputs ──\\n    # Input 0: Time from tone onset\\n    sample_start_times = f['acquisition']['BehavioralEvents']['sample_start_times']['timestamps'][:]\\n\\n    # Input 1: Photostim active\\n    photostim_intervals = get_photostim_intervals(f, n_trials_total, go_start_times, trial_start_times)\\n\\n    input_data = []\\n    for ti, trial_idx in enumerate(trial_indices):\\n        go_t = go_times[ti]\\n\\n        # Time from tone onset\\n        tone_onset = find_tone_onset_for_trial(sample_start_times, go_t)\\n        tone_onset_rel_go = tone_onset - go_t\\n        time_from_tone = BIN_CENTERS - tone_onset_rel_go  # seconds since tone onset\\n\\n        # Photostim binary time series\\n        photostim_ts = np.zeros(N_BINS, dtype=np.float32)\\n        ps_interval = photostim_intervals[trial_idx]\\n        if ps_interval is not None:\\n            onset_rel, offset_rel = ps_interval\\n            photostim_ts[(BIN_CENTERS >= onset_rel) & (BIN_CENTERS < offset_rel)] = 1.0\\n\\n        trial_input = np.stack([time_from_tone.astype(np.float32), photostim_ts], axis=0)  # (2, n_bins)\\n        input_data.append(trial_input)\\n\\n    # ── Outputs ──\\n    # Filtered trial data\\n    trial_outcomes = outcome[trial_indices]\\n    trial_early_lick = early_lick[trial_indices]\\n    trial_instructions = trial_instruction[trial_indices]\\n\\n    # Tongue y position\\n    tongue_ts = f['acquisition']['BehavioralTimeSeries']['Camera0_side_TongueTracking']['timestamps'][:]\\n    tongue_data_raw = f['acquisition']['BehavioralTimeSeries']['Camera0_side_TongueTracking']['data'][:]\\n\\n    tongue_discretized, p40, p60 = compute_tongue_y_all_trials(\\n        tongue_ts, tongue_data_raw, go_times, BIN_EDGES)\\n\\n    output_data = []\\n    for ti in range(n_trials):\\n        # Choice: 0=left, 1=right, 2=no_lick\\n        out = trial_outcomes[ti]\\n        inst = trial_instructions[ti]\\n        if out == 'hit':\\n            choice = 0 if inst == 'left' else 1\\n        elif out == 'miss':\\n            choice = 1 if inst == 'left' else 0  # opposite of instruction\\n        else:  # ignore\\n            choice = 2\\n\\n        # Outcome: 0=ignore, 1=miss, 2=hit\\n        outcome_val = {'ignore': 0, 'miss': 1, 'hit': 2}[out]\\n\\n        # Early lick: 0=no, 1=yes\\n        early_val = 0 if trial_early_lick[ti] == 'no early' else 1\\n\\n        # Tongue y: time-varying (n_bins,)\\n        tongue_y_disc = tongue_discretized[ti]\\n\\n        # Stack per-trial outputs with time-varying tongue\\n        # Per-trial values broadcast to all time points\\n        trial_output = np.stack([\\n            np.full(N_BINS, choice, dtype=np.int64),\\n            np.full(N_BINS, outcome_val, dtype=np.int64),\\n            np.full(N_BINS, early_val, dtype=np.int64),\\n            tongue_y_disc,\\n        ], axis=0)  # (4, n_bins)\\n        output_data.append(trial_output)\\n\\n    f.close()\\n\\n    elapsed = time.time() - t0\\n    print(f\\\"  {basename}: {n_good} good units, {n_trials} trials, perf={performance:.1%}, time={elapsed:.1f}s\\\")\\n\\n    # ── Processing visualization ──\\n    if show_processing:\\n        plot_processing(basename, neural_data, input_data, output_data,\\n                       go_times, BIN_CENTERS, good_regions, trial_outcomes, trial_instructions)\\n\\n    return {\\n        'subject_id': subject_id,\\n        'session_name': basename,\\n        'neural': neural_data,\\n        'input': input_data,\\n        'output': output_data,\\n        'brain_regions': good_regions,\\n        'n_good_units': n_good,\\n        'n_trials': n_trials,\\n        'performance': performance,\\n    }\\n\\n\\ndef plot_processing(basename, neural_data, input_data, output_data,\\n                    go_times, bin_centers, regions, outcomes, instructions):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Plot processing steps for visual verification.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 3, figsize=(18, 16))\\n    fig.suptitle(f'Processing: {basename}', fontsize=14)\\n\\n    n_trials = len(neural_data)\\n\\n    # 1. Neural activity heatmap for first trial\\n    ax = axes[0, 0]\\n    if n_trials > 0:\\n        trial_neural = neural_data[0]\\n        im = ax.imshow(trial_neural[:min(50, trial_neural.shape[0])], aspect='auto',\\n                       extent=[bin_centers[0], bin_centers[-1], 0, min(50, trial_neural.shape[0])],\\n                       cmap='viridis')\\n        ax.set_xlabel('Time (s)')\\n        ax.set_ylabel('Neuron')\\n        ax.set_title('Neural: Trial 0')\\n        ax.axvline(0, color='r', linestyle='--', label='Go cue')\\n        plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label='FR (Hz)')\\n\\n    # 2. Mean firing rate across trials\\n    ax = axes[0, 1]\\n    if n_trials > 0:\\n        all_rates = np.array([nd.mean(axis=0) for nd in neural_data])\\n        ax.plot(bin_centers, all_rates.mean(axis=0))\\n        ax.fill_between(bin_centers,\\n                        all_rates.mean(axis=0) - all_rates.std(axis=0),\\n                        all_rates.mean(axis=0) + all_rates.std(axis=0), alpha=0.3)\\n        ax.axvline(0, color='r', linestyle='--')\\n        ax.set_xlabel('Time (s)')\\n        ax.set_ylabel('Mean FR (Hz)')\\n        ax.set_title('Population avg FR')\\n\\n    # 3. Brain region distribution\\n    ax = axes[0, 2]\\n    from collections import Counter\\n    reg_counts = Counter(regions)\\n    regs = sorted(reg_counts.keys())\\n    ax.barh(range(len(regs)), [reg_counts[r] for r in regs])\\n    ax.set_yticks(range(len(regs)))\\n    ax.set_yticklabels(regs, fontsize=7)\\n    ax.set_xlabel('Count')\\n    ax.set_title('Brain regions')\\n\\n    # 4. Time from tone onset for a few trials\\n    ax = axes[1, 0]\\n    for i in range(min(5, n_trials)):\\n        ax.plot(bin_centers, input_data[i][0], alpha=0.5, label=f'Trial {i}')\\n    ax.axvline(0, color='r', linestyle='--')\\n    ax.set_xlabel('Time (s)')\\n    ax.set_ylabel('Time from tone (s)')\\n    ax.set_title('Input: Time from tone onset')\\n    ax.legend(fontsize=6)\\n\\n    # 5. Photostim for a few trials\\n    ax = axes[1, 1]\\n    for i in range(min(10, n_trials)):\\n        if input_data[i][1].max() > 0:\\n            ax.plot(bin_centers, input_data[i][1] + i * 0.1, alpha=0.7)\\n    ax.axvline(0, color='r', linestyle='--')\\n    ax.set_xlabel('Time (s)')\\n    ax.set_title('Input: Photostim active')\\n\\n    # 6. Outcome distribution\\n    ax = axes[1, 2]\\n    outcome_vals = [od[1, 0] for od in output_data]  # per-trial outcome\\n    unique, counts = np.unique(outcome_vals, return_counts=True)\\n    ax.bar(unique, counts)\\n    ax.set_xticks([0, 1, 2])\\n    ax.set_xticklabels(['ignore', 'miss', 'hit'])\\n    ax.set_title('Output: Outcome distribution')\\n\\n    # 7. Choice distribution\\n    ax = axes[2, 0]\\n    choice_vals = [od[0, 0] for od in output_data]\\n    unique, counts = np.unique(choice_vals, return_counts=True)\\n    ax.bar(unique, counts)\\n    ax.set_xticks([0, 1, 2])\\n    ax.set_xticklabels(['left', 'right', 'no_lick'])\\n    ax.set_title('Output: Choice distribution')\\n\\n    # 8. Early lick distribution\\n    ax = axes[2, 1]\\n    early_vals = [od[2, 0] for od in output_data]\\n    unique, counts = np.unique(early_vals, return_counts=True)\\n    ax.bar(unique, counts)\\n    ax.set_xticks([0, 1])\\n    ax.set_xticklabels(['no', 'yes'])\\n    ax.set_title('Output: Early lick distribution')\\n\\n    # 9. Tongue y discretized for a few trials\\n    ax = axes[2, 2]\\n    for i in range(min(5, n_trials)):\\n        ax.plot(bin_centers, output_data[i][3] + i * 0.1, alpha=0.5)\\n    ax.axvline(0, color='r', linestyle='--')\\n    ax.set_xlabel('Time (s)')\\n    ax.set_title('Output: Tongue y discretized')\\n\\n    # 10. Trial count summary\\n    ax = axes[3, 0]\\n    ax.text(0.1, 0.8, f'Total trials: {n_trials}', transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=12)\\n    ax.text(0.1, 0.6, f'Neurons: {neural_data[0].shape[0] if n_trials > 0 else 0}', transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=12)\\n    ax.text(0.1, 0.4, f'Time bins: {N_BINS}', transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=12)\\n    ax.set_title('Summary')\\n    ax.axis('off')\\n\\n    # 11-12. Empty\\n    axes[3, 1].axis('off')\\n    axes[3, 2].axis('off')\\n\\n    fig.tight_layout()\\n    session_id = basename.replace('.nwb', '')\\n    fig.savefig(f'processing_{session_id}.png', dpi=100)\\n    plt.close(fig)\\n\\n\\ndef main():\\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Convert MAP dataset to decoder format')\\n    parser.add_argument('outfile', type=str, help='Output pickle file path')\\n    parser.add_argument('--full', action='store_true', default=True, help='Process all sessions (default)')\\n    parser.add_argument('--sample', action='store_true', help='Process only 2 sessions for testing')\\n    parser.add_argument('--show-processing', action='store_true', help='Plot processing visualizations')\\n    args = parser.parse_args()\\n\\n    if args.sample:\\n        args.full = False\\n\\n    # Find all NWB files\\n    nwb_files = sorted(glob.glob('/app/data/sub-*/*.nwb'))\\n    print(f\\\"Found {len(nwb_files)} NWB files\\\")\\n\\n    if args.sample:\\n        # Pick files from different subjects to ensure diversity\\n        # Use files that are likely to pass session criteria\\n        sample_files = []\\n        seen_subjects = set()\\n        for nf in nwb_files:\\n            subj = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(nf))\\n            if subj not in seen_subjects:\\n                seen_subjects.add(subj)\\n                sample_files.append(nf)\\n            if len(sample_files) >= 5:  # try up to 5 to get at least 2 passing\\n                break\\n        nwb_files = sample_files\\n        print(f\\\"Sample mode: processing up to {len(nwb_files)} files\\\")\\n\\n    # Process all sessions\\n    all_sessions = []\\n    t_total_start = time.time()\\n\\n    for i, nwb_file in enumerate(nwb_files):\\n        print(f\\\"[{i+1}/{len(nwb_files)}] Processing {os.path.basename(nwb_file)}...\\\")\\n        try:\\n            result = process_session(nwb_file, show_processing=args.show_processing)\\n            if result is not None:\\n                all_sessions.append(result)\\n        except Exception as e:\\n            print(f\\\"  ERROR processing {nwb_file}: {e}\\\")\\n            import traceback\\n            traceback.print_exc()\\n\\n    t_total = time.time() - t_total_start\\n    print(f\\\"\\\\nProcessed {len(all_sessions)} sessions in {t_total:.1f}s ({t_total/max(len(all_sessions),1):.1f}s/session)\\\")\\n\\n    if len(all_sessions) == 0:\\n        print(\\\"ERROR: No sessions processed successfully!\\\")\\n        sys.exit(1)\\n\\n    # cuneate',\\\\n]\\\\n\\\\nCEREBELLUM_KEYWORDS = [\\\\n    'Cerebellum', 'cerebellum', 'Cerebellar',\\\\n    'Purkinje', 'Lobul', 'Flocculus',\\\\n    'Fastigial', 'Interposed', 'Dentate nucleus',\\\\n    'Nodulus', 'Uvula', 'Vermis',\\\\n    'Paraflocculus', 'Copula',\\\\n    'Ansiform', 'Simple lobule',\\\\n    'Central lobule', 'Culmen', 'Decliv',\\\\n    'Folium', 'Tuber', 'Pyramid',\\\\n    'Lingula',\\\\n]\\\\n\\\\nHIPPOCAMPUS_KEYWORDS = [\\\\n    'Hippocampus', 'hippocampus', 'Field CA',\\\\n    'Dentate gyrus', 'Subiculum', 'Entorhinal',\\\\n    'Fasciola cinerea', 'Indusium griseum',\\\\n]\\\\n\\\\nOLFACTORY_KEYWORDS = [\\\\n    'Olfactory', 'olfactory', 'Piriform',\\\\n    'Taenia tecta', 'Dorsal peduncular',\\\\n    'Anterior olfactory', 'Main olfactory',\\\\n    'Accessory olfactory',\\\\n]\\\\n\\\\nCORTICAL_SUBPLATE_KEYWORDS = [\\\\n    'Claustrum', 'Endopiriform',\\\\n    'Lateral amygdalar', 'Basolateral amygdalar',\\\\n    'Basomedial amygdalar', 'Posterior amygdalar',\\\\n    'Cortical amygdalar', 'Medial amygdalar',\\\\n    'Central amygdalar', 'Anterior amygdalar',\\\\n    'Intercalated', 'Amygdala',\\\\n]\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef classify_brain_region(anno_name):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Classify a detailed CCF annotation into a major brain region.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    if not anno_name or anno_name == '':\\\\n        return 'unknown'\\\\n\\\\n    # Check specific mappings first\\\\n    for prefix, region in MAJOR_REGION_MAP.items():\\\\n        if anno_name.startswith(prefix):\\\\n            return region\\\\n\\\\n    # Check keyword-based groups\\\\n    for kw in THALAMUS_KEYWORDS:\\\\n        if kw in anno_name:\\\\n            return 'TH'\\\\n    for kw in MIDBRAIN_KEYWORDS:\\\\n        if kw in anno_name:\\\\n            return 'MB'\\\\n    for kw in PONS_KEYWORDS:\\\\n        if kw in anno_name:\\\\n            return 'Pons'\\\\n    for kw in MEDULLA_KEYWORDS:\\\\n        if kw in anno_name:\\\\n            return 'MY'\\\\n    for kw in CEREBELLUM_KEYWORDS:\\\\n        if kw in anno_name:\\\\n            return 'CB'\\\\n    for kw in HIPPOCAMPUS_KEYWORDS:\\\\n        if kw in anno_name:\\\\n            return 'HPF'\\\\n    for kw in OLFACTORY_KEYWORDS:\\\\n        if kw in anno_name:\\\\n            return 'OLF'\\\\n    for kw in CORTICAL_SUBPLATE_KEYWORDS:\\\\n        if kw in anno_name:\\\\n            return 'CTXsp'\\\\n\\\\n    # Cortex catch-all (layer annotations)\\\\n    if 'layer' in anno_name.lower() or 'Layer' in anno_name:\\\\n        return 'CTX_other'\\\\n\\\\n    # Striatum catch-all\\\\n    if 'striatum' in anno_name.lower() or 'Striatum' in anno_name:\\\\n        return 'STR'\\\\n\\\\n    return 'unknown'\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef extract_unit_spike_times(spike_times_data, spike_times_index, unit_indices):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Extract spike times for multiple units at once.\\\\n    Returns list of arrays, one per unit.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    starts = np.zeros(len(unit_indices), dtype=np.int64)\\\\n    ends = spike_times_index[unit_indices].astype(np.int64)\\\\n    for i, idx in enumerate(unit_indices):\\\\n        if idx == 0:\\\\n            starts[i] = 0\\\\n        else:\\\\n            starts[i] = int(spike_times_index[idx - 1])\\\\n    return [spike_times_data[starts[i]:ends[i]] for i in range(len(unit_indices))]\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef compute_firing_rates_fast(unit_spike_times_list, go_times, bin_edges):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Compute firing rates for all units and trials.\\\\n    Optimized: iterate over units (outer) and vectorize across trials.\\\\n    Returns list of (n_units, n_bins) arrays, one per trial.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    n_units = len(unit_spike_times_list)\\\\n    n_bins = len(bin_edges) - 1\\\\n    bin_width = bin_edges[1] - bin_edges[0]\\\\n    n_trials = len(go_times)\\\\n\\\\n    # Pre-allocate result as 3D array, then split\\\\n    all_rates = np.zeros((n_units, n_trials, n_bins), dtype=np.float32)\\\\n\\\\n    for ni in range(n_units):\\\\n        st = unit_spike_times_list[ni]\\\\n        if len(st) == 0:\\\\n            continue\\\\n\\\\n        for ti in range(n_trials):\\\\n            go_t = go_times[ti]\\\\n            t_lo = go_t + bin_edges[0]\\\\n            t_hi = go_t + bin_edges[-1]\\\\n            i_lo = np.searchsorted(st, t_lo)\\\\n            i_hi = np.searchsorted(st, t_hi)\\\\n            if i_lo >= i_hi:\\\\n                continue\\\\n            # np.histogram is C-optimized and faster than searchsorted+add.at\\\\n            counts, _ = np.histogram(st[i_lo:i_hi], bins=bin_edges + go_t)\\\\n            all_rates[ni, ti] = counts\\\\n\\\\n    all_rates /= bin_width\\\\n\\\\n    # Split into list of per-trial arrays\\\\n    return [all_rates[:, ti, :] for ti in range(n_trials)]\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n# Task protocol defines fixed timing: sample epoch (0.65s) + delay (1.2s) = 1.85s before go cue.\\\\n# Early lick replays create extra sample_start events in the NWB data that confuse event-based\\\\n# matching (~12.5% of trials affected). Since the task timing is fixed, we use the protocol-defined\\\\n# offset for all trials.\\\\nTONE_ONSET_REL_GO = -1.85  # seconds before go cue\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef get_photostim_intervals(f, n_trials, go_times, trial_start_times):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Get photostim intervals relative to go cue for each trial.\\\\n    Returns list of (onset_rel, offset_rel) or None for each trial.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    photostim_onset = f['intervals']['trials']['photostim_onset'][:]\\\\n    photostim_dur = f['intervals']['trials']['photostim_duration'][:]\\\\n\\\\n    intervals = []\\\\n    for i in range(n_trials):\\\\n        if photostim_onset[i] == b'N/A':\\\\n            intervals.append(None)\\\\n        else:\\\\n            onset_rel_trial = float(photostim_onset[i])\\\\n            dur = float(photostim_dur[i])\\\\n            # Convert from trial-relative to go-cue-relative\\\\n            onset_abs = onset_rel_trial + trial_start_times[i]\\\\n            onset_rel_go = onset_abs - go_times[i]\\\\n            offset_rel_go = onset_rel_go + dur\\\\n            intervals.append((onset_rel_go, offset_rel_go))\\\\n    return intervals\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef compute_tongue_y_all_trials(tongue_ts, tongue_data, go_times, bin_edges,\\\\n                                 likelihood_thresh=TONGUE_LIKELIHOOD_THRESH):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Compute discretized tongue y-position for all trials using vectorized operations.\\\\n    Returns (tongue_discretized_list, p40, p60).\\\\n    Categories: 0=<40th, 1=40-60th, 2=>60th, 3=not visible\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    tongue_y = tongue_data[:, 1]\\\\n    tongue_lh = tongue_data[:, 2]\\\\n    n_bins = len(bin_edges) - 1\\\\n    n_trials = len(go_times)\\\\n    bin_width = bin_edges[1] - bin_edges[0]\\\\n\\\\n    # Pre-compute bin assignments for tongue timestamps\\\\n    # For each trial, we need tongue data in [go_time + T_START, go_time + T_END]\\\\n    # Use searchsorted for fast indexing\\\\n\\\\n    # First pass: collect visible y values for percentile computation\\\\n    visible_y_all = []\\\\n    # For each trial, find tongue data indices\\\\n    trial_tongue_ranges = []\\\\n    for ti in range(n_trials):\\\\n        go_t = go_times[ti]\\\\n        t_lo = go_t + bin_edges[0]\\\\n        t_hi = go_t + bin_edges[-1]\\\\n        i_lo = np.searchsorted(tongue_ts, t_lo)\\\\n        i_hi = np.searchsorted(tongue_ts, t_hi)\\\\n        trial_tongue_ranges.append((i_lo, i_hi))\\\\n\\\\n        if i_lo < i_hi:\\\\n            vis_mask = tongue_lh[i_lo:i_hi] >= likelihood_thresh\\\\n            if vis_mask.any():\\\\n                visible_y_all.append(tongue_y[i_lo:i_hi][vis_mask])\\\\n\\\\n    if len(visible_y_all) == 0:\\\\n        p40, p60 = None, None\\\\n        return [np.full(n_bins, 3, dtype=np.int64) for _ in range(n_trials)], p40, p60\\\\n\\\\n    all_visible = np.concatenate(visible_y_all)\\\\n    p40 = np.percentile(all_visible, 40)\\\\n    p60 = np.percentile(all_visible, 60)\\\\n\\\\n    # Second pass: discretize tongue y per trial and bin\\\\n    results = []\\\\n    for ti in range(n_trials):\\\\n        go_t = go_times[ti]\\\\n        i_lo, i_hi = trial_tongue_ranges[ti]\\\\n        trial_bins = np.full(n_bins, 3, dtype=np.int64)\\\\n\\\\n        if i_lo >= i_hi:\\\\n            results.append(trial_bins)\\\\n            continue\\\\n\\\\n        # Get tongue data for this trial\\\\n        trial_ts = tongue_ts[i_lo:i_hi]\\\\n        trial_y = tongue_y[i_lo:i_hi]\\\\n        trial_lh = tongue_lh[i_lo:i_hi]\\\\n\\\\n        # Assign each tongue sample to a bin\\\\n        rel_ts = trial_ts - go_t\\\\n        bin_idx = np.searchsorted(bin_edges, rel_ts, side='right') - 1\\\\n        valid = (bin_idx >= 0) & (bin_idx < n_bins)\\\\n\\\\n        if not valid.any():\\\\n            results.append(trial_bins)\\\\n            continue\\\\n\\\\n        bin_idx_v = bin_idx[valid]\\\\n        trial_y_v = trial_y[valid]\\\\n        trial_lh_v = trial_lh[valid]\\\\n\\\\n        # Compute mean y and mean likelihood per bin using bincount\\\\n        for b in range(n_bins):\\\\n            b_mask = bin_idx_v == b\\\\n            if not b_mask.any():\\\\n                continue\\\\n            avg_lh = trial_lh_v[b_mask].mean()\\\\n            if avg_lh >= likelihood_thresh:\\\\n                avg_y = trial_y_v[b_mask].mean()\\\\n                if avg_y < p40:\\\\n                    trial_bins[b] = 0\\\\n                elif avg_y <= p60:\\\\n                    trial_bins[b] = 1\\\\n                else:\\\\n                    trial_bins[b] = 2\\\\n\\\\n        results.append(trial_bins)\\\\n    return results, p40, p60\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef process_session(nwb_path, show_processing=False):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Process a single NWB session file.\\\\n    Returns session data dict or None if session should be skipped.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    t0 = time.time()\\\\n    basename = os.path.basename(nwb_path)\\\\n\\\\n    f = h5py.File(nwb_path, 'r')\\\\n\\\\n    # ── Subject info ──\\\\n    subject_id = f['general']['subject']['subject_id'][()].decode()\\\\n\\\\n    # ── Trial info ──\\\\n    n_trials_total = f['intervals']['trials']['id'].shape[0]\\\\n    outcome = np.array([x.decode() for x in f['intervals']['trials']['outcome'][:]])\\\\n    early_lick = np.array([x.decode() for x in f['intervals']['trials']['early_lick'][:]])\\\\n    trial_instruction = np.array([x.decode() for x in f['intervals']['trials']['trial_instruction'][:]])\\\\n    auto_water = f['intervals']['trials']['auto_water'][:]\\\\n    free_water = f['intervals']['trials']['free_water'][:]\\\\n    photostim_power = f['intervals']['trials']['photostim_power'][:]\\\\n    trial_start_times = f['intervals']['trials']['start_time'][:]\\\\n\\\\n    # ── Session selection ──\\\\n    # The DANDI archive already contains sessions selected by the paper authors\\\\n    # (performance > 65%, >= 50 correct L and R trials). One session has no good units.\\\\n    is_auto_or_free = (auto_water == 1) | (free_water == 1)\\\\n\\\\n    # Compute performance for metadata (on control non-early-lick trials)\\\\n    is_control = (photostim_power == b'N/A') & (early_lick == 'no early') & ~is_auto_or_free\\\\n    n_control_responded = np.sum((outcome[is_control] == 'hit') | (outcome[is_control] == 'miss'))\\\\n    n_correct = np.sum(outcome[is_control] == 'hit')\\\\n    performance = n_correct / n_control_responded if n_control_responded > 0 else 0\\\\n\\\\n    # ── Trial filtering: remove auto_water and free_water ──\\\\n    trial_mask = ~is_auto_or_free\\\\n    trial_indices = np.where(trial_mask)[0]\\\\n    n_trials = len(trial_indices)\\\\n\\\\n    if n_trials < 2:\\\\n        print(f\\\\\\\"  SKIP {basename}: only {n_trials} valid trials\\\\\\\")\\\\n        f.close()\\\\n        return None\\\\n\\\\n    # ── Go cue times ──\\\\n    go_start_times = f['acquisition']['BehavioralEvents']['go_start_times']['timestamps'][:]\\\\n    assert len(go_start_times) == n_trials_total, f\\\\\\\"Go cue count mismatch: {len(go_start_times)} vs {n_trials_total}\\\\\\\"\\\\n    go_times = go_start_times[trial_indices]\\\\n    trial_starts = trial_start_times[trial_indices]\\\\n\\\\n    # ── Good units ──\\\\n    classification = f['units']['classification'][:]\\\\n    good_mask = classification == b'good'\\\\n    good_indices = np.where(good_mask)[0]\\\\n    n_good = len(good_indices)\\\\n\\\\n    if n_good == 0:\\\\n        print(f\\\\\\\"  SKIP {basename}: no good units\\\\\\\")\\\\n        f.close()\\\\n        return None\\\\n\\\\n    # ── Brain region annotations ──\\\\n    anno_names = f['units']['anno_name'][:]\\\\n    good_annos = [anno_names[i].decode() if isinstance(anno_names[i], bytes) else str(anno_names[i])\\\\n                  for i in good_indices]\\\\n    good_regions = [classify_brain_region(a) for a in good_annos]\\\\n\\\\n    # ── Spike times ──\\\\n    spike_times_data = f['units']['spike_times'][:]\\\\n    spike_times_index = f['units']['spike_times_index'][:]\\\\n\\\\n    # Extract spike times for all good units once\\\\n    unit_spike_times = extract_unit_spike_times(spike_times_data, spike_times_index, good_indices)\\\\n\\\\n    # Compute firing rates for all good units and trials\\\\n    neural_data = compute_firing_rates_fast(unit_spike_times, go_times, BIN_EDGES)\\\\n\\\\n    # ── Inputs ──\\\\n    # Input 0: Time from tone onset\\\\n    sample_start_times = f['acquisition']['BehavioralEvents']['sample_start_times']['timestamps'][:]\\\\n\\\\n    # Input 1: Photostim active\\\\n    photostim_intervals = get_photostim_intervals(f, n_trials_total, go_start_times, trial_start_times)\\\\n\\\\n    input_data = []\\\\n    for ti, trial_idx in enumerate(trial_indices):\\\\n        go_t = go_times[ti]\\\\n\\\\n        # Time from tone onset\\\\n        tone_onset = find_tone_onset_for_trial(sample_start_times, go_t)\\\\n        tone_onset_rel_go = tone_onset - go_t\\\\n        time_from_tone = BIN_CENTERS - tone_onset_rel_go  # seconds since tone onset\\\\n\\\\n        # Photostim binary time series\\\\n        photostim_ts = np.zeros(N_BINS, dtype=np.float32)\\\\n        ps_interval = photostim_intervals[trial_idx]\\\\n        if ps_interval is not None:\\\\n            onset_rel, offset_rel = ps_interval\\\\n            photostim_ts[(BIN_CENTERS >= onset_rel) & (BIN_CENTERS < offset_rel)] = 1.0\\\\n\\\\n        trial_input = np.stack([time_from_tone.astype(np.float32), photostim_ts], axis=0)  # (2, n_bins)\\\\n        input_data.append(trial_input)\\\\n\\\\n    # ── Outputs ──\\\\n    # Filtered trial data\\\\n    trial_outcomes = outcome[trial_indices]\\\\n    trial_early_lick = early_lick[trial_indices]\\\\n    trial_instructions = trial_instruction[trial_indices]\\\\n\\\\n    # Tongue y position\\\\n    tongue_ts = f['acquisition']['BehavioralTimeSeries']['Camera0_side_TongueTracking']['timestamps'][:]\\\\n    tongue_data_raw = f['acquisition']['BehavioralTimeSeries']['Camera0_side_TongueTracking']['data'][:]\\\\n\\\\n    tongue_discretized, p40, p60 = compute_tongue_y_all_trials(\\\\n        tongue_ts, tongue_data_raw, go_times, BIN_EDGES)\\\\n\\\\n    output_data = []\\\\n    for ti in range(n_trials):\\\\n        # Choice: 0=left, 1=right, 2=no_lick\\\\n        out = trial_outcomes[ti]\\\\n        inst = trial_instructions[ti]\\\\n        if out == 'hit':\\\\n            choice = 0 if inst == 'left' else 1\\\\n        elif out == 'miss':\\\\n            choice = 1 if inst == 'left' else 0  # opposite of instruction\\\\n        else:  # ignore\\\\n            choice = 2\\\\n\\\\n        # Outcome: 0=ignore, 1=miss, 2=hit\\\\n        outcome_val = {'ignore': 0, 'miss': 1, 'hit': 2}[out]\\\\n\\\\n        # Early lick: 0=no, 1=yes\\\\n        early_val = 0 if trial_early_lick[ti] == 'no early' else 1\\\\n\\\\n        # Tongue y: time-varying (n_bins,)\\\\n        tongue_y_disc = tongue_discretized[ti]\\\\n\\\\n        # Stack per-trial outputs with time-varying tongue\\\\n        # Per-trial values broadcast to all time points\\\\n        trial_output = np.stack([\\\\n            np.full(N_BINS, choice, dtype=np.int64),\\\\n            np.full(N_BINS, outcome_val, dtype=np.int64),\\\\n            np.full(N_BINS, early_val, dtype=np.int64),\\\\n            tongue_y_disc,\\\\n        ], axis=0)  # (4, n_bins)\\\\n        output_data.append(trial_output)\\\\n\\\\n    f.close()\\\\n\\\\n    elapsed = time.time() - t0\\\\n    print(f\\\\\\\"  {basename}: {n_good} good units, {n_trials} trials, perf={performance:.1%}, time={elapsed:.1f}s\\\\\\\")\\\\n\\\\n    # ── Processing visualization ──\\\\n    if show_processing:\\\\n        plot_processing(basename, neural_data, input_data, output_data,\\\\n                       go_times, BIN_CENTERS, good_regions, trial_outcomes, trial_instructions)\\\\n\\\\n    return {\\\\n        'subject_id': subject_id,\\\\n        'session_name': basename,\\\\n        'neural': neural_data,\\\\n        'input': input_data,\\\\n        'output': output_data,\\\\n        'brain_regions': good_regions,\\\\n        'n_good_units': n_good,\\\\n        'n_trials': n_trials,\\\\n        'performance': performance,\\\\n    }\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef plot_processing(basename, neural_data, input_data, output_data,\\\\n                    go_times, bin_centers, regions, outcomes, instructions):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Plot processing steps for visual verification.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 3, figsize=(18, 16))\\\\n    fig.suptitle(f'Processing: {basename}', fontsize=14)\\\\n\\\\n    n_trials = len(neural_data)\\\\n\\\\n    # 1. Neural activity heatmap for first trial\\\\n    ax = axes[0, 0]\\\\n    if n_trials > 0:\\\\n        trial_neural = neural_data[0]\\\\n        im = ax.imshow(trial_neural[:min(50, trial_neural.shape[0])], aspect='auto',\\\\n                       extent=[bin_centers[0], bin_centers[-1], 0, min(50, trial_neural.shape[0])],\\\\n                       cmap='viridis')\\\\n        ax.set_xlabel('Time (s)')\\\\n        ax.set_ylabel('Neuron')\\\\n        ax.set_title('Neural: Trial 0')\\\\n        ax.axvline(0, color='r', linestyle='--', label='Go cue')\\\\n        plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label='FR (Hz)')\\\\n\\\\n    # 2. Mean firing rate across trials\\\\n    ax = axes[0, 1]\\\\n    if n_trials > 0:\\\\n        all_rates = np.array([nd.mean(axis=0) for nd in neural_data])\\\\n        ax.plot(bin_centers, all_rates.mean(axis=0))\\\\n        ax.fill_between(bin_centers,\\\\n                        all_rates.mean(axis=0) - all_rates.std(axis=0),\\\\n                        all_rates.mean(axis=0) + all_rates.std(axis=0), alpha=0.3)\\\\n        ax.axvline(0, color='r', linestyle='--')\\\\n        ax.set_xlabel('Time (s)')\\\\n        ax.set_ylabel('Mean FR (Hz)')\\\\n        ax.set_title('Population avg FR')\\\\n\\\\n    # 3. Brain region distribution\\\\n    ax = axes[0, 2]\\\\n    from collections import Counter\\\\n    reg_counts = Counter(regions)\\\\n    regs = sorted(reg_counts.keys())\\\\n    ax.barh(range(len(regs)), [reg_counts[r] for r in regs])\\\\n    ax.set_yticks(range(len(regs)))\\\\n    ax.set_yticklabels(regs, fontsize=7)\\\\n    ax.set_xlabel('Count')\\\\n    ax.set_title('Brain regions')\\\\n\\\\n    # 4. Time from tone onset for a few trials\\\\n    ax = axes[1, 0]\\\\n    for i in range(min(5, n_trials)):\\\\n        ax.plot(bin_centers, input_data[i][0], alpha=0.5, label=f'Trial {i}')\\\\n    ax.axvline(0, color='r', linestyle='--')\\\\n    ax.set_xlabel('Time (s)')\\\\n    ax.set_ylabel('Time from tone (s)')\\\\n    ax.set_title('Input: Time from tone onset')\\\\n    ax.legend(fontsize=6)\\\\n\\\\n    # 5. Photostim for a few trials\\\\n    ax = axes[1, 1]\\\\n    for i in range(min(10, n_trials)):\\\\n        if input_data[i][1].max() > 0:\\\\n            ax.plot(bin_centers, input_data[i][1] + i * 0.1, alpha=0.7)\\\\n    ax.axvline(0, color='r', linestyle='--')\\\\n    ax.set_xlabel('Time (s)')\\\\n    ax.set_title('Input: Photostim active')\\\\n\\\\n    # 6. Outcome distribution\\\\n    ax = axes[1, 2]\\\\n    outcome_vals = [od[1, 0] for od in output_data]  # per-trial outcome\\\\n    unique, counts = np.unique(outcome_vals, return_counts=True)\\\\n    ax.bar(unique, counts)\\\\n    ax.set_xticks([0, 1, 2])\\\\n    ax.set_xticklabels(['ignore', 'miss', 'hit'])\\\\n    ax.set_title('Output: Outcome distribution')\\\\n\\\\n    # 7. Choice distribution\\\\n    ax = axes[2, 0]\\\\n    choice_vals = [od[0, 0] for od in output_data]\\\\n    unique, counts = np.unique(choice_vals, return_counts=True)\\\\n    ax.bar(unique, counts)\\\\n    ax.set_xticks([0, 1, 2])\\\\n    ax.set_xticklabels(['left', 'right', 'no_lick'])\\\\n    ax.set_title('Output: Choice distribution')\\\\n\\\\n    # 8. Early lick distribution\\\\n    ax = axes[2, 1]\\\\n    early_vals = [od[2, 0] for od in output_data]\\\\n    unique, counts = np.unique(early_vals, return_counts=True)\\\\n    ax.bar(unique, counts)\\\\n    ax.set_xticks([0, 1])\\\\n    ax.set_xticklabels(['no', 'yes'])\\\\n    ax.set_title('Output: Early lick distribution')\\\\n\\\\n    # 9. Tongue y discretized for a few trials\\\\n    ax = axes[2, 2]\\\\n    for i in range(min(5, n_trials)):\\\\n        ax.plot(bin_centers, output_data[i][3] + i * 0.1, alpha=0.5)\\\\n    ax.axvline(0, color='r', linestyle='--')\\\\n    ax.set_xlabel('Time (s)')\\\\n    ax.set_title('Output: Tongue y discretized')\\\\n\\\\n    # 10. Trial count summary\\\\n    ax = axes[3, 0]\\\\n    ax.text(0.1, 0.8, f'Total trials: {n_trials}', transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=12)\\\\n    ax.text(0.1, 0.6, f'Neurons: {neural_data[0].shape[0] if n_trials > 0 else 0}', transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=12)\\\\n    ax.text(0.1, 0.4, f'Time bins: {N_BINS}', transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=12)\\\\n    ax.set_title('Summary')\\\\n    ax.axis('off')\\\\n\\\\n    # 11-12. Empty\\\\n    axes[3, 1].axis('off')\\\\n    axes[3, 2].axis('off')\\\\n\\\\n    fig.tight_layout()\\\\n    session_id = basename.replace('.nwb', '')\\\\n    fig.savefig(f'processing_{session_id}.png', dpi=100)\\\\n    plt.close(fig)\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef main():\\\\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Convert MAP dataset to decoder format')\\\\n    parser.add_argument('outfile', type=str, help='Output pickle file path')\\\\n    parser.add_argument('--full', action='store_true', default=True, help='Process all sessions (default)')\\\\n    parser.add_argument('--sample', action='store_true', help='Process only 2 sessions for testing')\\\\n    parser.add_argument('--show-processing', action='store_true', help='Plot processing visualizations')\\\\n    args = parser.parse_args()\\\\n\\\\n    if args.sample:\\\\n        args.full = False\\\\n\\\\n    # Find all NWB files\\\\n    nwb_files =
